intent.raw_query: Morocco Marrakech and Sahara, $1000 solo, 7 days, March 2026

selected_hotel.name: Djemaa el-Fna, Medina, Marrakech Boutique Stay

experiences.name: Explore Djemaa el-Fna Square
experiences.description: Immerse yourself in the beating heart of Marrakech at this UNESCO-listed square. Watch snake charmers, storytellers, and musicians by day, then witness the square transform into a massive open-air food market at sunset with dozens of stalls serving harira soup, grilled meats, and fresh orange juice.

experiences.name: Sahara Desert Camel Trek & Overnight Camp
experiences.description: Ride camels into the golden Erg Chebbi dunes near Merzouga for a truly transformative adventure. Spend the night in a traditional Berber camp under an extraordinary canopy of stars, enjoy live Gnawa music around a campfire, and wake before dawn to witness one of the world's most breathtaking sunrises over the dunes.
experiences.location: Erg Chebbi Dunes, Merzouga, Sahara Desert

experiences.name: Medina Souks & Tanneries Walking Tour
experiences.description: Navigate the labyrinthine medieval souks of Marrakech's ancient medina, discovering artisan workshops producing leather goods, lanterns, spices, and textiles. Visit the famous Chouara-style tanneries from a rooftop vantage point to observe the centuries-old leather dyeing process still practiced today.

experiences.name: Bahia Palace & Saadian Tombs Historical Tour
experiences.description: Step back into Morocco's imperial past with a self-guided tour of the stunning 19th-century Bahia Palace, featuring intricate zellij tilework, carved cedarwood ceilings, and lush courtyards. Continue to the nearby Saadian Tombs, a hidden royal necropolis dating to the 16th century rediscovered only in 1917.

experiences.name: Traditional Moroccan Cooking Class
experiences.description: Join a local chef in a riad kitchen for a hands-on cooking class where you'll learn to prepare authentic Moroccan dishes such as lamb tagine with preserved lemons, bastilla, and fresh mint tea. Begin with a guided visit to the spice market to select ingredients, gaining deep insight into Moroccan culinary culture and traditions.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Morocco (Marrakech and Sahara)
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

hotel.name: Djemaa el-Fna, Medina, Marrakech Boutique Stay

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Marrakech Menara Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Take bus #19 or a shared taxi (petit taxi) from the airport to your riad in Djemaa el-Fna Medina (~30–50 MAD). Check in, freshen up, and get oriented.
day_by_day.afternoon: First immersion into Djemaa el-Fna square — the beating heart of Marrakech. Wander the square, watch street performers, snake charmers, and storytellers. Stroll into the nearby souks (Souk Semmarine) for a sensory introduction to the medina. Free to explore.
day_by_day.evening: Watch the magical sunset transformation of Djemaa el-Fna as food stalls light up and the square comes alive. Grab a spot on the rooftop terrace of Café de France or Café Argana for a mint tea with panoramic views (~20–30 MAD). Then explore the night market on foot.

meals.breakfast: Eat on the plane or grab a snack at the airport upon arrival.
meals.lunch: Quick bite near the airport or at a local café in the medina after check-in — try a msemen (Moroccan flatbread) with amlou (argan-almond dip) for ~15–20 MAD.
meals.dinner: Djemaa el-Fna food stalls — try harira soup (10 MAD), grilled merguez sausages, and Moroccan salads. Full meal for ~40–60 MAD at stall numbers 1–30 in the square.

day_by_day.notes: Bus #19 from the airport is the cheapest option (~20 MAD). Agree on taxi fares before getting in. Keep your valuables secure in the busy square. Exchange some cash at the airport or a medina bureau de change (avoid hotel exchange rates).

day_by_day.morning: Visit the iconic Koutoubia Mosque gardens (exterior only for non-Muslims) — free. Then head to the Bahia Palace, a stunning 19th-century Moroccan palace with intricate tilework and carved cedarwood ceilings (~70 MAD entry). Arrive early to beat the crowds.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Mellah (Jewish Quarter) and the ruins of the El Badi Palace (~70 MAD entry) — a once-magnificent 16th-century palace now hauntingly beautiful in its decay. Rooftop views over the medina are superb. Afterward, visit the Saadian Tombs (~70 MAD) — royal tombs dating to the 16th century, just a 5-minute walk away.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the medina for a deep dive into the souks — Souk des Teinturiers (dyers' souk), Souk Cherratine (leather), and Souk Haddadine (blacksmiths). Bargaining is expected and part of the culture. End the evening with a relaxing walk back to Djemaa el-Fna.

meals.breakfast: At your riad if included, or visit a local bakery (farran) near the medina for khobz bread, olive oil, and mint tea — ~15–25 MAD.
meals.lunch: Cheap and delicious lunch at Restaurant Chez Bahia near the Bahia Palace — tagine or couscous for ~50–70 MAD.
meals.dinner: Try a sit-down local restaurant in the medina such as Restaurant Al Baraka or similar — 3-course Moroccan set menu for ~80–100 MAD. Avoid tourist-trap restaurants on the square perimeter.

day_by_day.notes: A combined ticket for Bahia Palace, El Badi Palace, and Saadian Tombs can sometimes be purchased — ask at the first site. Wear comfortable shoes as the medina streets are uneven cobblestone. Modest dress is recommended near religious sites.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to the Palmeraie and Majorelle Garden. Take a petit taxi to Majorelle Garden (~20–30 MAD one way) — the stunning cobalt-blue garden designed by Jacques Majorelle and later owned by Yves Saint Laurent (~150 MAD entry, includes the Berber Museum). Visit early to avoid crowds.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to the Musée de Marrakech (housed in a beautiful 19th-century palace, ~50 MAD) and the nearby Ben Youssef Medersa (~70 MAD) — one of the finest examples of Islamic architecture in Morocco with intricate zellige tilework and carved stucco. Both are in the northern medina.
day_by_day.evening: Hammam experience — visit a traditional public hammam (hammam Bab Doukkala or Hammam Mouassine) for an authentic local scrub (~50–80 MAD for the basic experience). Afterward, relax at a rooftop café with views over the medina rooftops.

meals.breakfast: Café des Épices near Place Rahba Kedima — café au lait and Moroccan pancakes (baghrir) for ~30–40 MAD.
meals.lunch: Picnic-style lunch near Majorelle Garden — buy fresh fruit, olives, bread, and cheese from a local épicerie (grocery) for ~30–40 MAD total.
meals.dinner: Street food dinner in the medina — try a makouda (potato fritter) sandwich, bissara (fava bean soup), and fresh orange juice from Djemaa el-Fna. Full meal for ~30–50 MAD.

day_by_day.notes: Majorelle Garden is a 20-minute walk or short taxi from the medina. Book the hammam in the late afternoon for a quieter experience. The Ben Youssef Medersa and Musée de Marrakech are walking distance from each other — plan them together.

day_by_day.morning: Depart Marrakech early (6:00–7:00 AM) on a shared CTM or Supratours bus or a pre-booked budget group tour toward the Sahara Desert via the Draa Valley route (Ouarzazate direction). The journey to Merzouga (gateway to Erg Chebbi dunes) takes approximately 8–10 hours by bus or 9–10 hours total with stops. Book in advance (~150–200 MAD by CTM bus to Ouarzazate, then onward connection).
day_by_day.afternoon: En route, pass through the dramatic Tizi n'Tichka mountain pass (2,260m) in the High Atlas Mountains — breathtaking scenery. Stop briefly at Aït Benhaddou, a UNESCO World Heritage ksar (fortified village) used in Game of Thrones and Gladiator filming. Walk around the exterior or cross the river for ~10–20 MAD entry.
day_by_day.evening: Continue toward Ouarzazate or push on to Boumalne Dades or Tinghir for an overnight budget guesthouse stop if doing the journey independently (~100–150 MAD for a basic room). Alternatively, if on a budget group tour, arrive at a desert camp near Merzouga by evening.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at your riad before departure — or grab a coffee and msemen from a street stall near the bus station (~20 MAD).
meals.lunch: Roadside Berber restaurant near Aït Benhaddou — tagine set menu for ~60–80 MAD. Negotiate before ordering.
meals.dinner: Simple dinner at your guesthouse or a local restaurant in Ouarzazate or Tinghir — harira, bread, and a tagine for ~50–70 MAD.

day_by_day.notes: The cheapest way to reach the Sahara is by public CTM/Supratours bus, but it requires multiple connections and an overnight stop. A budget group tour (booked in Marrakech) typically costs 400–700 MAD per person for a 2-day/1-night Sahara trip and includes transport, camel ride, and desert camp — often better value. Book 1–2 days in advance from medina tour agencies.

day_by_day.morning: Arrive at Merzouga and the Erg Chebbi sand dunes by mid-morning (if continuing from previous night's stop). Check into a budget desert auberge or bivouac camp (~150–250 MAD per person including dinner and breakfast). Explore the edge of the dunes on foot and watch the shifting light on the orange sands.
day_by_day.afternoon: Camel trek into the Erg Chebbi dunes — a 1–2 hour guided camel ride into the desert (~150–200 MAD per person, negotiable). Reach a nomadic-style desert camp deep in the dunes. Relax, climb the highest dunes for panoramic views, and watch the golden hour light paint the desert.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset from the top of the dunes — one of Morocco's most spectacular sights. Return to camp for a traditional Berber dinner around a campfire with live Gnawa music and drumming. Sleep under a sky full of stars in a traditional desert tent (included in camp package).

meals.breakfast: Simple breakfast at the guesthouse before heading to Merzouga — bread, jam, argan oil, mint tea (~included or ~20–30 MAD).
meals.lunch: Light lunch at a Merzouga auberge before the camel trek — omelette, salad, and bread for ~40–60 MAD.
meals.dinner: Traditional Berber dinner at the desert camp — included in most camp packages. Expect tagine, couscous, flatbread, and mint tea around the fire.

day_by_day.notes: March weather in the Sahara is ideal — warm days (25–30°C) and cool nights (10–15°C). Bring a warm layer for the night. Sandstorm risk is low but pack a scarf for the camel ride. Bargain respectfully for camel rides and camp packages — prices are negotiable. Avoid the most touristy camps closest to the road; walk 15–20 minutes deeper into the dunes for more authentic options.

day_by_day.morning: Wake before sunrise (around 6:30 AM in March) for the magical desert dawn — watch the sun rise over the dunes from your tent or a nearby ridge. Sunrise camel ride back to the auberge. Freshen up and enjoy a Berber breakfast before departure.
day_by_day.afternoon: Begin the return journey to Marrakech. If on a group tour, transport is included. If independent, take a shared taxi or local bus from Merzouga to Rissani, then onward connections. Optional stop at the Todra Gorge (Gorges du Todra) — dramatic 300m-high rock canyon perfect for a short hike along the river (~free to enter, guided hike ~50–100 MAD). Stunning scenery and great for photos.
day_by_day.evening: Continue driving back through the Draa Valley and High Atlas. Arrive in Ouarzazate or push toward Marrakech (arriving late evening ~10–11 PM). If exhausted, overnight in a budget guesthouse in Ouarzazate (~100–150 MAD).

meals.breakfast: Included at the desert camp — mint tea, bread, honey, and Berber omelette.
meals.lunch: Lunch stop at Todra Gorge — small restaurant serving tagine and salad for ~60–80 MAD with a view of the gorge.
meals.dinner: Dinner in Ouarzazate or a roadside restaurant on the return — kefta (spiced meatball) tagine and bread for ~50–70 MAD.

day_by_day.notes: The Todra Gorge detour adds 1–2 hours but is highly recommended for adventure and nature lovers. If returning by group tour, confirm the itinerary includes Todra or Dades Gorge. Keep some cash on hand as ATMs are scarce in the desert region — Ouarzazate has reliable ATMs.

day_by_day.morning: Return to Marrakech (if not already back). Spend the morning revisiting any missed medina highlights — the tanneries of the Chouara district (view from leather shop rooftops, free with soft purchase pressure), or the peaceful Cyber Parc Arsat Moulay Abdeslam gardens for a relaxing stroll (free). Last-minute souvenir shopping in the souks — argan oil, leather goods, spices, and Berber jewelry.
day_by_day.afternoon: Relax at your riad and prepare for departure. If time allows, visit the Musée de la Photographie de Marrakech (~30 MAD) or climb the rooftop of Le Jardin Secret (~50 MAD) for a final aerial view of the medina. Pack, check out, and head to the airport. Airport bus #19 or petit taxi (~50–70 MAD).
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Marrakech Menara Airport. Arrive 2–3 hours early for international flights. Final mint tea or fresh orange juice (5 MAD) from a medina juice stall before heading out.

meals.breakfast: Final Moroccan breakfast at your riad or a local café — msemen, honey, argan oil, hard-boiled eggs, and mint tea for ~25–40 MAD.
meals.lunch: Farewell lunch at a well-regarded budget restaurant — try Café Clock Marrakech (cultural hub, burgers and Moroccan fusion ~60–90 MAD) or a traditional derb restaurant for a final tagine.
meals.dinner: Light snack or meal at the airport if departing in the evening, or grab a final street food bite from Djemaa el-Fna before heading to the airport.

day_by_day.notes: Budget summary estimate for 7 days: Accommodation ~700–1,000 MAD total; Transport (airport + buses + shared taxis) ~400–600 MAD; Desert tour (group) ~500–700 MAD; Entry fees ~500 MAD; Food ~800–1,200 MAD; Extras/souvenirs ~200–400 MAD. Grand total approximately 3,100–3,900 MAD (~$300–380 USD) excluding flights. Always carry small change (1–5 MAD coins) for tips, public toilets, and market haggling.

trip_options.title: Classic Morocco (Marrakech and Sahara) Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

hotel.name: Djemaa el-Fna, Medina, Marrakech Boutique Stay

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — flight arrives at 13:00
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Marrakech Menara Airport at 13:00. Clear customs, collect luggage, and take a pre-booked taxi or airport transfer (~150–200 MAD) to your riad in Djemaa el-Fna Medina. Check in, freshen up, and take a gentle orientation stroll through the immediate lanes of the Medina to get your bearings. Peek into the edges of Djemaa el-Fna square without diving in fully — save the magic for tonight.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Djemaa el-Fna as the sun sets and the square transforms into a spectacular open-air spectacle. Watch snake charmers, acrobats, storytellers, and musicians. Browse the food stalls that light up after dark for a lively first Moroccan dinner experience.

meals.breakfast: On the plane or at the airport
meals.lunch: Grab a quick bite near the airport or at a café close to the riad upon arrival — try a simple harira soup and msemen flatbread at a local café for ~30–50 MAD
meals.dinner: Eat at the Djemaa el-Fna food stalls (Stall No. 1 or Stall 14 are reliable favourites) — try grilled merguez sausages, kefta brochettes, and fresh orange juice for ~80–120 MAD per person

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 light on activities. Jet lag and travel fatigue are real. Drink bottled water, keep valuables secure in the busy square, and confirm your Sahara transport or tour booking for later in the trip tonight while relaxing at the riad.

day_by_day.morning: After a traditional Moroccan breakfast at your riad, head out early (9:00 AM) to explore the historic Koutoubia Mosque and its gardens — the minaret is a landmark of Islamic architecture (non-Muslims view from outside). Then walk north through the Medina souks: Souk Semmarine (textiles), Souk des Teinturiers (dyers), and the leather tanneries viewable from nearby rooftop terraces. Bargaining is expected — enjoy the process.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the stunning Bahia Palace (entry ~70 MAD), a 19th-century masterpiece of Moroccan craftsmanship with intricate zellige tilework, carved cedar ceilings, and lush courtyards. Afterwards, explore the nearby Mellah (Jewish Quarter) and the ornate El Badi Palace ruins (entry ~70 MAD) — climb the ramparts for sweeping views over Marrakech.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Djemaa el-Fna for sunset. Climb to a rooftop café terrace (Café de France or Café Glacier) for mint tea with panoramic views over the square. Then dine at a proper Medina restaurant for a full traditional Moroccan feast.

meals.breakfast: Riad breakfast — typically includes msemen, amlou (almond-argan dip), honey, fresh orange juice, and mint tea (usually included or ~60–80 MAD)
meals.lunch: Lunch at Nomad Restaurant near the Mellah — modern Moroccan cuisine, excellent pastilla and tagines, ~120–180 MAD per person
meals.dinner: Dinner at Le Foundouk or Dar Zitoun — atmospheric candlelit riad restaurant serving a 3-course Moroccan menu with bastilla, lamb tagine, and pastilla au lait for ~200–280 MAD per person

day_by_day.notes: Wear comfortable walking shoes — the Medina streets are uneven cobblestone. Hire a licensed guide from the tourist office (~300–400 MAD for a half-day) if you want deeper historical context for the souks and palaces. Avoid unofficial 'guides' who approach you on the street.

day_by_day.morning: Start with a visit to the Saadian Tombs (entry ~70 MAD) — a hidden 16th-century royal necropolis rediscovered in 1917, featuring beautifully preserved mausoleums. Then walk to the Musée de Marrakech housed in a gorgeous 19th-century palace (entry ~50 MAD) to see Moroccan art, manuscripts, and decorative arts. End the morning at the Ben Youssef Madrasa (entry ~70 MAD), one of North Africa's largest Islamic schools with breathtaking carved stucco and cedar woodwork.
day_by_day.afternoon: Escape the Medina bustle with a visit to Jardin Majorelle (entry ~150 MAD) — the iconic cobalt-blue garden created by French painter Jacques Majorelle and later restored by Yves Saint Laurent. The adjacent Berber Museum is included in the ticket. Alternatively, visit Menara Gardens for a free, peaceful lakeside stroll with Atlas Mountain backdrop. Return for a traditional hammam experience — try Hammam de la Rose or a local neighbourhood hammam (~150–300 MAD for a full scrub and massage).
day_by_day.evening: Relaxed evening in the Medina. Browse evening souks for souvenirs — argan oil, leather goods, spices, and lanterns. Enjoy a leisurely dinner in the Mouassine neighbourhood.

meals.breakfast: Riad breakfast
meals.lunch: Light lunch at Café du Livre or Café Arabe in the Mouassine district — salads, sandwiches, and fresh juices, ~100–150 MAD per person
meals.dinner: Dinner at Riad Yima (run by artist Hassan Hajjaj) or Shéhérazade — colourful, artsy atmosphere with solid Moroccan home-style cooking, ~150–220 MAD per person

day_by_day.notes: Book Jardin Majorelle tickets online in advance — it sells out, especially on weekends. The hammam is best done in the late afternoon as a wind-down ritual. Bring flip-flops and a change of clothes. March weather in Marrakech is pleasant (18–24°C) — a light layer for evenings is recommended.

day_by_day.morning: Early start — depart Marrakech by 7:00–8:00 AM with a shared or private 4WD tour vehicle heading toward Merzouga and the Sahara Desert. The journey (~9–10 hours driving) crosses the dramatic High Atlas Mountains via the Tizi n'Tichka pass (2,260m). Stop at the pass for photos of snow-dusted peaks and Berber villages. Continue to the ancient fortified ksar (village) of Aït Benhaddou — a UNESCO World Heritage Site used as a film set for Gladiator, Game of Thrones, and Lawrence of Arabia.
day_by_day.afternoon: Spend 1.5–2 hours exploring Aït Benhaddou on foot — climb through the mud-brick kasbah layers to the granary at the top for panoramic views over the Draa Valley. This is one of Morocco's most photogenic historic sites. Continue driving southeast through the Valley of Roses (Vallée du Dadès) and the dramatic Gorges du Dadès if time allows, passing through Ouarzazate (the 'Hollywood of Africa').
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Merzouga (gateway to Erg Chebbi dunes) around 17:00–18:00. Meet your camel handlers at the edge of the dunes. Mount camels and ride ~45–60 minutes into the heart of the Sahara to your desert camp, arriving just in time for a golden sunset over the towering orange dunes. Settle into your camp under a canopy of stars.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the riad before departure — pack snacks and water for the road
meals.lunch: Stop for lunch in Ouarzazate or at a roadside restaurant in the Draa Valley — Berber tagine and bread, ~80–120 MAD per person
meals.dinner: Traditional Berber dinner at the desert camp — harira soup, slow-cooked lamb or chicken tagine, Moroccan salads, and mint tea around a campfire with live Gnawa music (~included in most mid-range camp packages)

day_by_day.notes: Book a reputable mid-range desert camp in advance — look for camps offering private or semi-private Berber tents with proper beds, clean shared bathrooms, and electricity (e.g., Luxury Desert Camp Merzouga or similar). The camel ride is approximately 1 hour each way — it can be bumpy; wear long trousers. Bring a warm layer — desert nights in March drop to 5–10°C. Bring a headlamp, sunscreen, and a scarf for dust.

day_by_day.morning: Wake before sunrise (~6:00 AM) and climb the nearest high dune on foot to watch the Sahara sunrise — one of the most extraordinary experiences of the trip. The shifting colours from deep purple to burning orange over the sea of dunes is unforgettable. Return to camp for a Berber breakfast. After breakfast, explore the dune landscape on foot, try sandboarding down the steep dune faces (boards available at camp), or take a guided 4WD excursion into the deeper desert to visit nomadic Berber families and ancient fossil beds.
day_by_day.afternoon: Rest during the hottest part of the day (12:00–15:00) at camp — read, nap, or simply absorb the extraordinary silence of the desert. In the late afternoon, take a longer guided walk or quad bike ride (~150–250 MAD rental) through the dune corridors as the light softens. Visit the small Merzouga village on the edge of the dunes to see the local way of life and browse small artisan shops selling fossils, minerals, and Tuareg jewellery.
day_by_day.evening: Second night at the desert camp. Enjoy a bonfire dinner under a sky so dense with stars that the Milky Way is clearly visible. Participate in a Gnawa drumming and music session — these hypnotic rhythms are a core part of Saharan Berber culture. Stargaze with fellow travellers before sleeping.

meals.breakfast: Camp breakfast — Berber mint tea, msemen flatbread, honey, argan oil, hard-boiled eggs, and fresh fruit (included in camp)
meals.lunch: Light lunch at camp — salads, bread, and tagine leftovers or a simple prepared meal (included in camp)
meals.dinner: Second campfire dinner — often a mechoui (slow-roasted lamb) or couscous night at mid-range camps (included in camp package)

day_by_day.notes: Protect your camera and phone from fine sand with a zip-lock bag or dedicated case. The sandboarding is best on the steeper north-facing dunes — camp staff will point you in the right direction. Drink at least 2–3 litres of water throughout the day. The quad bikes are a fun afternoon option but negotiate price beforehand. Tipping camel handlers and camp staff is customary (20–50 MAD per person per service).

day_by_day.morning: Final sunrise camel ride or dune walk at dawn. After breakfast, mount camels for the return ride back to Merzouga. Depart by 8:30–9:00 AM for the long return drive to Marrakech. Take an alternative northern route through the stunning Todra Gorge — a dramatic 300-metre-high limestone canyon carved by the Todra River. Stop to walk through the narrowest section of the gorge (free entry) and have tea at one of the small cafés nestled in the canyon walls.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue west through the Ziz Valley and its vast palm grove oasis — one of the most scenic drives in Morocco. Stop at Tinghir for lunch. Push on through the Draa Valley, passing ancient kasbahs and ksour (fortified villages) crumbling beautifully into the desert landscape. Rejoin the main road and begin the Atlas crossing back toward Marrakech, arriving in the early evening.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive back in Marrakech around 18:00–19:00. Check back into your riad, shower off the desert dust, and head to Djemaa el-Fna for a final evening in the square. Treat yourself to a slightly more indulgent farewell dinner at one of Marrakech's better restaurants.

meals.breakfast: Final camp breakfast before departure
meals.lunch: Lunch in Tinghir or at a roadside restaurant in the Todra Gorge area — fresh trout (a local speciality from the gorge river), Berber tagine, and mint tea, ~80–120 MAD per person
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at La Maison Arabe or Dar Yacout — iconic upscale-mid riad restaurants with live music, elaborate Moroccan feasts, and beautiful courtyards, ~250–350 MAD per person

day_by_day.notes: The Todra Gorge stop adds about 1 hour to the journey but is absolutely worth it — one of Morocco's most dramatic natural landscapes. If energy is low from the desert, skip the gorge and take the direct route back. Confirm your riad has kept your room or re-book in advance. The return drive is long (~9–10 hours with stops) — bring a good playlist, snacks, and a neck pillow.

day_by_day.morning: Leisurely final morning in Marrakech. After a slow riad breakfast, do any last-minute souvenir shopping in the souks — this is your best chance to pick up quality items you may have spotted earlier: handwoven Berber rugs, hand-stamped leather bags, saffron, ras el hanout spice blends, and argan oil products. Visit the Ensemble Artisanal (government-run fixed-price craft centre near the Koutoubia) if you want fair prices without bargaining stress.
day_by_day.afternoon: Spend the early afternoon at the peaceful Cyber Parc Arsat Moulay Abdeslam — a free public garden near the Medina walls, perfect for a quiet final stroll. Alternatively, revisit any favourite spot from the week. Begin packing and check out of the riad by the agreed time (usually 12:00). Store luggage at the riad (most will hold bags until your departure). Head to the airport with ample time — allow 45–60 minutes from the Medina to the airport by taxi.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Marrakech Menara Airport. Reflect on an extraordinary week spanning ancient imperial cities, Berber mountain passes, and the infinite silence of the Sahara.

meals.breakfast: Final riad breakfast — savour the mint tea and msemen one last time
meals.lunch: Farewell lunch at Café des Épices in the spice square (Place Rahba Kedima) — rooftop terrace with Medina views, excellent salads, briouats, and fresh juices, ~100–150 MAD per person
meals.dinner: Airport meal or early dinner near the riad before transfer — a simple bowl of harira soup and chebakia pastry at a local café as a final Moroccan taste, ~40–60 MAD

day_by_day.notes: Allow extra time for souk shopping on the final morning — it is easy to lose track of time in the labyrinthine lanes. Negotiate taxi fares to the airport firmly (official rate ~150–200 MAD from the Medina) or use a ride-hailing app like Careem. Keep a small amount of MAD for airport tips and last purchases. Declare any argan oil over 100ml in checked luggage. This has been a beautifully balanced trip — culture, history, adventure, and the desert all woven together across 7 unforgettable days in Morocco.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Morocco (Marrakech and Sahara) Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

hotel.name: Djemaa el-Fna, Medina, Marrakech Boutique Stay

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Marrakech Menara Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Private luxury transfer arranged to your boutique riad in the Medina near Djemaa el-Fna. Check-in, freshen up, and settle into your accommodations.
day_by_day.afternoon: Gentle orientation walk through Djemaa el-Fna square with a private local guide. Explore the edges of the iconic square, observe the storytellers, musicians, and snake charmers, and stroll into the first lanes of the souks for a sensory introduction to Marrakech. Visit the nearby Koutoubia Mosque gardens for a peaceful first impression of the city's architecture.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset rooftop aperitif at a terrace overlooking Djemaa el-Fna as the square transforms into its legendary night market. Watch the food stalls ignite and the square fill with life from above before descending for a curated private dinner.

meals.breakfast: Not applicable (mid-day arrival)
meals.lunch: Welcome light mezze and mint tea at your riad upon check-in — prepared by the in-house team as a private arrival experience
meals.dinner: Dinner at Le Foundouk, a refined Moroccan-French restaurant in the Medina offering candlelit ambiance, heritage architecture, and dishes such as lamb pastilla and preserved lemon chicken tagine

day_by_day.notes: Arrival day is intentionally relaxed. Avoid heavy sightseeing to allow acclimatization. Ensure your riad concierge briefs you on the week ahead and confirms all private transfers and guides.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided tour of the Bahia Palace and El Badi Palace ruins. Begin at Bahia Palace, a 19th-century masterpiece of Moroccan craftsmanship with painted cedar ceilings, zellij tilework, and lush interior gardens. Continue to the atmospheric ruins of El Badi Palace, built by Sultan Ahmad al-Mansur, where storks nest atop crumbling ramparts and underground chambers can be explored.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Mellah (Jewish Quarter) and the historic Saadian Tombs. The Saadian Tombs, rediscovered in 1917, house the ornately decorated mausoleums of the Saadian dynasty. Afterward, browse the Mellah's spice market and artisan workshops with your guide, followed by a private hands-on Moroccan cooking class at a traditional riad kitchen — learn to prepare harira soup, bastilla, and msemen.
day_by_day.evening: Private hammam and spa ritual at a luxury heritage hammam such as Les Bains de Marrakech or Royal Mansour Spa (day pass). Traditional black soap scrub, ghassoul clay mask, and argan oil massage. Return to the Medina for a late dinner.

meals.breakfast: Elaborate Moroccan breakfast at your riad — fresh msemen flatbreads, argan oil honey, amlou almond paste, fresh-squeezed orange juice, Moroccan mint tea, and seasonal fruit
meals.lunch: Lunch at Nomad Restaurant, a stylish rooftop spot near the spice souks offering modern Moroccan cuisine with panoramic Medina views — try the lamb merguez and Moroccan salad platters
meals.dinner: Dinner at Dar Yacout, a legendary Marrakech institution inside a 17th-century palace — multi-course Moroccan feast with live Gnawa music, candlelit courtyards, and rooftop cocktails

day_by_day.notes: Book the Saadian Tombs early in the afternoon to avoid peak crowds. Confirm hammam appointment in advance as luxury slots fill quickly.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided visit to the Madrasa Ben Youssef, one of the most stunning examples of Islamic architecture in North Africa, featuring intricate stucco carvings, cedar woodwork, and a serene marble courtyard. Continue to the Museum of Marrakech housed in the 19th-century Mnebhi Palace, exploring its collection of Moroccan art, manuscripts, and ceramics.
day_by_day.afternoon: Immersive souk exploration with a private master artisan guide — visit the dyers' quarter (Souk Sebbaghine), the leather tannery viewpoints, the lantern makers, and the carpet weavers. Participate in a private carpet-weaving or zellige tile-making workshop with a master craftsman. End with a curated shopping session for high-quality Moroccan crafts with your guide's authentication assistance.
day_by_day.evening: Exclusive private dinner in a secret garden setting — arrange through your riad concierge for a private table at La Mamounia's Le Marocain restaurant, set within the legendary hotel's Moorish gardens. Alternatively, a private rooftop dinner arranged by your riad under the stars with a personal chef.

meals.breakfast: Riad breakfast with additions of beghrir (semolina crepes), local honey varieties, and freshly baked khobz bread
meals.lunch: Lunch at Café Arabe, a multi-level Medina institution with Italian-Moroccan fusion cuisine and a beautiful rooftop — try the kefta cigars and fresh Moroccan salads
meals.dinner: Le Marocain at La Mamounia Hotel — one of Morocco's most celebrated dining rooms with impeccable Moroccan haute cuisine, live traditional music, and extraordinary interior design

day_by_day.notes: The souk experience is best done with a trusted private guide to avoid unsolicited pressure from vendors. Your riad can arrange a reputable licensed guide. Confirm La Mamounia reservation at least 48 hours in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Depart Marrakech by private luxury 4x4 vehicle toward the Sahara Desert via the dramatic Dades Valley and Draa Valley route. Pass through the High Atlas Mountains, stopping at the Tizi n'Tichka pass (2,260m) for panoramic mountain photography. Continue through Ouarzazate, the 'Door of the Desert,' for a brief stop at the UNESCO-listed Aït Benhaddou ksar — a breathtaking fortified mud-brick village used in films such as Gladiator and Game of Thrones.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the scenic drive through the Valley of Roses (Vallée des Roses) and the dramatic Todra Gorge — towering 300-meter limestone canyon walls perfect for photography and a short walk along the canyon floor. Continue toward Merzouga and the Erg Chebbi dunes, arriving in the late afternoon as the desert light turns golden.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Merzouga. Mount private camels for a guided sunset trek into the Erg Chebbi dunes — the highest sand dunes in Morocco, reaching up to 150 meters. Arrive at your exclusive luxury desert camp (such as Scarabeo Camp or Erg Chebbi Luxury Camp) as the stars emerge. Private Gnawa and Berber musicians perform around a desert fire.

meals.breakfast: Early riad breakfast before departure — packed with energy-rich foods for the long drive
meals.lunch: Lunch stop at a curated traditional restaurant in Ouarzazate or near Aït Benhaddou — slow-cooked lamb tagine with prunes and almonds, served in a courtyard setting
meals.dinner: Private candlelit dinner under the Sahara stars at your luxury desert camp — traditional Berber feast including harira soup, mechoui (whole-roasted lamb), couscous, and Moroccan pastries with desert mint tea ceremony

day_by_day.notes: This is a long driving day (approximately 8–9 hours total with stops). Depart Marrakech no later than 07:30. Ensure your private driver is confirmed the evening before. Bring layers as desert nights in March can drop to 5–10°C.

day_by_day.morning: Pre-dawn wake-up for a private guided sunrise camel or 4x4 dune ascent to the highest accessible dune crest for a spectacular Sahara sunrise. Return to camp for a traditional Berber breakfast. Optional: sandboarding down the dunes or a guided quad-bike excursion across the erg with a professional Berber guide.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a traditional Berber nomad family encampment arranged privately through your camp — share tea, learn about nomadic desert life, and hear stories of desert navigation passed down through generations. Explore the fossil and meteorite markets near Merzouga (this region is one of the world's richest meteorite discovery zones). Optional: private falconry demonstration in the desert.
day_by_day.evening: Second night at the luxury desert camp. Private stargazing session with a telescope and an astronomer guide — the Erg Chebbi skies offer some of the darkest and clearest conditions in North Africa. Return to camp for a Moroccan mezze dinner and Berber storytelling around the fire.

meals.breakfast: Traditional Berber desert breakfast at camp — khobz with olive oil and za'atar, hard-boiled eggs, fresh dates, argan oil, and multiple rounds of sweet mint tea
meals.lunch: Light camp lunch of Moroccan salads, fresh bread, grilled kefta, and seasonal fruit
meals.dinner: Second desert camp dinner — themed around Tuareg-Berber cuisine with slow-cooked goat tagine, saffron-infused couscous, and honey-drenched chebakia pastries

day_by_day.notes: Sunrise is approximately 07:15 in mid-March — wake-up call should be set for 05:45. Sunscreen and a wide-brim hat are essential for daytime dune activities. Sandstorms are rare in March but pack a light scarf for wind protection.

day_by_day.morning: Depart the desert camp after breakfast and begin the scenic return journey toward Marrakech via the Ziz Valley and Erfoud. Stop at the Erfoud fossil workshops where artisans craft objects from 350-million-year-old Devonian marine fossils unique to this region. Continue through the Ziz Gorges and the stunning date palm oasis of the Tafilalet — one of the largest palm groves in Morocco.
day_by_day.afternoon: Stop in Tinghir to visit the Todra Gorge once more from a different vantage point, or continue to the Dades Gorge for a walk among the 'Monkey Fingers' rock formations. Optional stop at a traditional argan oil cooperative run by Berber women en route back through the Atlas foothills — participate in the hand-pressing process and purchase premium cold-pressed argan oil directly.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive back in Marrakech by early evening. Freshen up at your riad. Spend the final evening leisurely exploring Djemaa el-Fna at night — hire a private guide for a curated night market experience, sampling street food with a discerning eye, watching acrobats and musicians, and ending with a rooftop drink overlooking the illuminated square.

meals.breakfast: Final desert camp breakfast before departure
meals.lunch: Lunch at a scenic roadside restaurant in the Dades or Ziz Valley — lamb mechoui, fresh Berber bread, and local olive varieties with Atlas mountain views
meals.dinner: Dinner at Pepe Nero, a sophisticated Marrakech restaurant blending Italian and Moroccan influences in a stunning riad setting — ideal for a relaxed penultimate evening with excellent wine selection

day_by_day.notes: The return drive is approximately 7–8 hours with stops. Aim to be back in Marrakech by 19:00. Use the drive time to rest — your driver can make comfort stops as needed. Confirm any final-day reservations or experiences with your riad concierge upon return.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Marrakech — visit the serene Majorelle Garden, designed by French painter Jacques Majorelle and later restored by Yves Saint Laurent. Explore the cobalt-blue villa, exotic botanical collection, and the outstanding Musée Yves Saint Laurent Marrakech (YSL Museum) adjacent to the gardens — a world-class museum dedicated to the designer's life and his deep connection to Morocco.
day_by_day.afternoon: Last-minute curated luxury shopping in the Gueliz district (Marrakech's modern French quarter) — visit high-end Moroccan design boutiques such as 33 Rue Majorelle (YSL's former concept store), Intensité Nomade, and Kulchi for premium Moroccan fashion, leather goods, and home décor. Return to riad for final packing and a farewell hammam or spa treatment.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner at one of Marrakech's finest tables. Private transfer to Marrakech Menara Airport for departure (confirm flight time and arrange transfer accordingly with your concierge).

meals.breakfast: Grand farewell riad breakfast — the full spread including all Moroccan specialties enjoyed throughout the week, with a special pastry selection from a nearby artisan patisserie
meals.lunch: Lunch at Grand Café de la Poste in Gueliz — a colonial-era brasserie with excellent Moroccan-French cuisine, perfect for a relaxed final afternoon
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at Restaurant 68 or the rooftop restaurant at La Mamounia — celebrate the journey with a premium multi-course tasting menu, Moroccan wine pairings, and a toast to the Marrakech skyline

day_by_day.notes: Confirm departure transfer timing with your riad at least the night before. Marrakech Menara Airport is approximately 15–20 minutes from the Medina. Allow extra time for luggage with desert souvenirs. Keep a small bag accessible for airport essentials. Tip your riad staff, private guide, and driver generously — it is customary and greatly appreciated.
